sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 both sit at the bottom of their trailing one-month range, closing Sep 15 at 7,585.73 and 28,937.84 after a steady multi-day slide from early-September highs near 7,748 and 29,544. The VIX has climbed alongside, closing at 17.20 — near the top of its own one-month band and up from a mid-14 reading two weeks earlier — consistent with a gradual drift rather than a sharp dislocation. Euro Stoxx 50 shows the same pattern, also at its one-month low. Against that backdrop, the week ahead carries a light load: just 7 tracked reports spread across consumer-cyclical, industrials, consumer-defensive, and technology names, with no single sector dominating the calendar.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Mon: AZO US and THO US both report into consumer-cyclical, a sector running about flat over recent prints (-0.15% median 3-day reaction across 497 tickers). Tue: CTAS US and PAYX US report into industrials, this week's weakest group at -1.48% median (604 tickers), while GIS US reports into consumer-defensive at -0.56% median (362 tickers). Wed: COST US closes out consumer-defensive for the week and SNX US reports into technology, the only sector in this week's pool with a positive median reaction (+0.87% across 567 tickers). None of this week's names fall in the strongest-reacting sectors — mining, alternative-asset-management, and copper lead that table but have no reports due in this window.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Mining leads the reaction table at +6.62% median (172 tickers, 2,630 news items — a thick information flow), followed by alternative-asset-management at +2.925% (6 tickers, 232 items) and copper at +2.63% (6 tickers, 248 items). None of this week's reporting names sit in these three sectors, so the strongest signals this week are carried over from names that already reported rather than from this week's calendar.
